title: PRD: Differential Sampling, Precision Ladders, and Triggered Remediation for Optimize
creator: Maya Patel
description: Purpose: Define an actionable PRD that specifies differential prompt sampling, precision ladder thresholds, and a triggered remediation/rollback lifecycle for Optimize evals. This will reduce false positives from long-tail drift, ensure that customer-facing cohorts have tighter tolerances, and provide deterministic rollback actions when composite signals cross predefined boundaries.
scope:
- Implement differential sampling matrix (by cohort: enterprise, pro, free, long-tail) for prompt collection and sentinel injection.
- Define composite signal and scoring function used by Optimize to decide regressions.
- Establish precision ladder thresholds (Tier 0..3) and corresponding remediation actions (auto-fix, traffic throttle, full rollback).
- Draft A/B and canary rules for staged rollouts tied to these thresholds.
- Instrument dashboards and automated alerts for the defined signals.
out_of_scope:
- Changes to runtime kernel heuristics or low-level batching logic (separate infra RFC).
- New human labeling tooling (we will use existing labeling pipelines).
- Billing policy changes tied to rolling back releases.
requirements:
1) Sampling matrix: differential rates, minimum per-cohort daily ingestion, and adversarial sentinel injection policy.
2) Composite signal: quality_score (0-100 automated proxy) + regression_penalty (latency/cost delta) + safety_flag (binary).
3) Precision ladder: define Tier 0 (no action) to Tier 3 (immediate rollback) numeric boundaries and time windows.
4) A/B criteria: statistical decision rules (Bayesian sequential with 95% posterior credible interval for uplift > MDE).
5) Rollback actions: automated throttles, canary rescues, and full traffic rollback with audit log entries and postmortem triggers.
6) Minimum sample size constraints per cohort for decisions (see acceptance criteria).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Sampling matrix implemented: enterprise cohort sampled at 100% of production prompts for the first 7 days of canary, pro at 30%, free at 5%, long-tail oversample by factor 3 for rare patterns; documented in sampling spec and visible in dashboard.

A2: Composite signal computed for every prompt and stored with timestamp; signal components (quality_score, latency_delta, safety_flag) are shown in per-cohort dashboards within 15 minutes of ingestion.

A3: Precision ladder thresholds established and documented: Tier 1 (minor regression) = composite drop >= 3 points for 24h; Tier 2 (material) = drop >= 7 points for 6h; Tier 3 (critical) = drop >= 12 points for 1h OR any safety_flag true for >1% of sampled prompts in 30m.

A4: A/B test engine integrated with Bayesian sequential test: can detect MDE of 3% uplift with 95% posterior probability on aggregated metric; experiments enforce minimum N per cohort (enterprise 2000 prompts, pro 1000, free 500, long-tail 1500 unique prompts sampled).

A5: Automatic remediation actions wired: Tier 1 -> create priority ticket + email and raise non-blocking alert; Tier 2 -> pause rollout progression and throttle traffic to 10% for 30m with auto-recheck; Tier 3 -> initiate immediate full rollback to pinned model version and create incident bridge with oncall paging. Each action must be logged with user-visible rationale in rollout history.

A6: Safety guardrail: any run with safety_flag true for >0.1% of enterprise-cohort prompts triggers an immediate canary-stop irrespective of composite score and opens review workflow (manual approval to continue), with audit log entry referencing the trigger.
A7: Dashboards: per-cohort time series for composite signal, component breakdown, sample counts, and MDE-confidence bands; alerts configured in PagerDuty with runbook links.
metrics_and_signals: quality_score: automated proxy combining ngram overlap, semantic rerank score, and periodic human-labeled calibration (0-100)
latency_delta: percent change in p95 relative to baseline release
safety_flag: binary from safety probes / policy classifier
traffic_weight_by_cohort: current live weight assigned to candidate, control during ramp
trigger_definitions: adversarial_sentinel_trigger: injected hot prompts that target known failure modes; if failure rate > 20% of sentinels in 1h, escalate to Tier 2
long_tail_resonance: oversampled cohort drift where long-tail sample quality_score median decreases by 8 points vs baseline over 24h
cohort_isolation_spike: a single customer cohort shows a >15% composite drop relative to global baseline for 3 consecutive hours
experiment_design: Primary design: sequential Bayesian A/B with hierarchical cohort model. Start: 5% traffic to candidate for 12h; evaluate composite signal and cohort deltas. Ramp to 20% if no Tier2+ triggers for 24h; ramp to 50% then 100% following same windows. Control pinned to baseline model version. Each stage enforces minimum N by cohort before decision. Rescue canary: if candidate passes global but fails enterprise cohort, route enterprise traffic back to control while allowing general population to continue on candidate.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal canary: 0%->5% (12h) -> 20% (24h) with full sampling and sentinel injection.
2) Staged public ramp: 20%->50%->100% with automated checks at each stage.
3) If Tier2 condition observed: automatic ramp pause + 1-hr diagnostic window; if unresolved escalate to Tier3 rollback.
4) Post-rollback: create postmortem, freeze related deploys, and require signoff from PM+Eng+Safety to reattempt.
5) Provide 'rescue canary' knob for targeted cohort rollback without global rollback.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Oversampling long-tail increases label and storage costs; tradeoff accepted to reduce false positives in long-tail regression detection.
Strict enterprise thresholds can increase rollbacks and churn; mitigation: rescue canary to protect public traffic while stabilizing enterprise experience.
Automated rollback reduces time-to-recovery but can cause oscillations if thresholds are too tight; plan to monitor oscillation rate and widen thresholds if persistent flapping observed.
Dependence on automated quality proxy requires regular calibration with human labels; plan monthly calibration jobs and alerts for proxy drift.
